interface.name: lege_shell_manager_v1
interface.description: Bound only by the client the compositor itself launched as the shell.

request.name: show_all_windows

description.summary: recovery view: every window, scattered across active outputs on the Recovery layer, with no reliance on the shell to compute the layout

request.description: Also compositor-keybinding-reachable with no shell running at all (`compositor/FORK.md`); this request exists so the shell can offer the same action from its own UI.

request.name: escape_fullscreen_or_modal

description.summary: compositor-level way out of a fullscreen or modal window

request.description: `toplevel` null escapes whichever window currently holds activation, if any. Also compositor-keybinding-reachable with no shell running (`docs/architecture/accessibility.md`).

request.name: set_layer_surface

description.summary: declare which typed layer a shell surface belongs to

request.description: Only `shell_overlay`, `notification`, `home_surface` and `system_modal` are valid here — `secure_lock` and `recovery` are compositor-owned and refused even for the shell; a client-side window's own layer (`normal` / `app_on_top`) is set through xdg-shell, not this request.

request.name: set_exclusive_zone

description.summary: reserve space along one edge of the output a shell surface is on

request.description:
A dock or panel asks for `size` logical pixels along `edge`, so that ordinary windows are placed beside it rather than beneath it. The compositor recomputes the affected output's work area (`lege_window::work_area_for`) and repairs any window this displaces.
This is a request, not an instruction. `lege_window::Output::usable` refuses a claim that would swallow the output, or that would leave too little room for a window's recovery band — the shell is a restartable, replaceable process and does not get the last word on whether the user can reach their windows. A refused claim is silently ignored rather than erroring: a shell that asked for too much should still run, just without its reservation.
`size` of 0 releases a previously reserved zone. Reservations are per surface, so a surface that is destroyed releases its own automatically.

arg.name: size
arg.summary: logical pixels along that edge; 0 releases
